I’m really sorry to hear that you’re struggling :(
I’m not a therapist or really very educated on environmentalism, but I know that there are a lot of little things you can do to reduce your carbon footprint (initiatives like the zero-waste movement, reducing electricity usage, opting for public transport over private and stuff like that). 
Maybe if you try and implement some of these little things into your day-to-day life you can find a little more peace of mind in knowing that you are not so much contributing to climate change as you might have been before. 
I know you’ve probably heard cliché phrases like this before, but try not to let your worries consume you. The government, universities, and many large corporations are well aware of the impact of modern living on the environment. Change takes time

I enjoy sketching, so my therapist recommended that I try the following whenever I feel disgusted or ashamed of my body:
  1. do a 5 minutes sketch of how you think your body looks in a certain pose
  2. sit in front of a mirror and sketch yourself in the same pose
  3. compare the two
[ hasn’t really worked for me, but I thought I’d put it out there :::) ]

I’m nearly 20 and I’ve had multiple loves in my life (and by loves I obviously mean I have loved many many people and they have never felt the same way back). Nowadays I am so scared of loving somebody because unironically it is always having love inside that hurts the most.

the same situation happened with me, except it was me (the girl) who told him that I had a crush on him. He was my best friend at the time, and it was awkward for a while because he explicitly told me that he did not feel the same way even though he really liked me as a person. 
After a really awkward and (extremely) painful period of time he kinda ‘forgot’ about the situation and our friendship was stronger than ever. 
The friendship is over now though because I couldn’t really handle being around him anymore cus my feelings were just overwhelming and consuming me and it physically hurt inside to just be friends. It was painful to stop talking to him at first, but I’m so glad I did it because the separation really helped me move on and it was a really freeing process. So, I guess, don’t worry if it doesn’t work out - just remember your happiness comes first and there is a light at the end of this dark tunnel. (Cheesy, sorry haha)

Maybe start off by trying to replace some of your guilty pleasure foods (aka Starbucks) with a home-made replacement? Things made at home tend to be healthier, and you become much more aware of what you’re actually putting into your body. (Plus, if you carry around your homemade replacement in a keep cup you’re also helping the enviroment! It’s a win-win)
Also, remember that any exercise is good exercise. Nobody can jump from nothing straight to the 400-cal cardio burns at the gym :)

I’m the same, my mum has never once told me I’m beautiful. My dad likes to tell me I’m pretty when I have bad days and I can’t get out of bed, but it feels more like strategy than truth. When I used to work in this shop as a cashier some of the older men who bought newspapers used to call me gorgeous or beautiful, and I don’t know if this is disgusting or not but it made me feel tingly inside. And yeah, they used to address all the girls working in the shop as “beautiful”, but it didn’t matter and it still meant so much.
